chapters.title: Chapter 1: How Business Income Gets Taxed in India

lessons.title: Why Tax Is a Business Decision, Not Just a Compliance Chore

body.text: Most of a company's tax bill is decided long before anyone files a return. It is decided when the business picks a structure, signs a vendor, grants ESOPs, plans its cash flow and chooses a tax regime. By filing season, the accountant is mostly just writing down the result.

children.text: Ask a first-time founder what tax means for their business and you will usually hear some version of "that's the CA's job in July." That view is expensive. For a profitable Indian company, tax on profit alone takes roughly a quarter to a third of every rupee earned before tax. Add GST on sales, TDS on payments and payroll taxes, and tax touches almost every transaction the business makes.
This lesson makes one argument: tax is a cost you manage, like rent or salaries, not a form you fill. Once you see it that way, the rest of this course becomes a toolkit rather than a rulebook.
The Taxes a Business Actually Meets

markDefs.definition: A tax paid by the person or entity that earns the income and cannot be passed on to someone else, such as income tax on a company's profit.
A tax collected on transactions (sales, imports) that is ultimately borne by the final consumer, such as GST or customs duty.

children.text: Indian business taxes fall into two families.
Direct taxes
are levied on what the business earns.
Indirect taxes
are levied on what the business sells or imports, and are collected from customers. Both show up on the same bank statement.

body.text: Notice that TDS and GST make your business a collection agent for the government. The money is not yours, but the penalty for mishandling it is. That is why a payments clerk or an HR executive can create a tax problem as easily as the CFO.

children.text: Proof That Tax Moves Value: 20 September 2019

If you doubt that tax is a value driver, look at what happened on a single Friday in 2019. Before markets opened, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that domestic companies could opt for a base corporate tax rate of 22%, down from 30%, provided they gave up most exemptions and incentives. Nothing about any company's sales, margins or products changed that morning. Only the share of profit going to the government did.

stats.label: Old headline effective rate
stats.context: 30% base + 12% surcharge + 4% cess, large domestic company

stats.label: Sensex move that day
stats.context: Its biggest single-day gain in about a decade

children.text: Investors did the maths instantly. If a company pays about 10 percentage points less of its profit as tax, profit after tax rises by roughly 15% with no operational change at all (74.83 divided by 65.06 is about 1.15). Markets repriced that extra profit within hours.

body.title: Effective corporate tax rate by regime (income above ₹10 crore)
Quick Check: The 2019 Cut
body.question: A company earns ₹100 of profit before tax. By roughly how much does its profit after tax rise when its effective tax rate falls from 34.94% to 25.17%?
options: It does not change, because pre-tax profit is the same
body.explanation: Profit after tax moves from ₹65.06 (100 minus 34.94) to ₹74.83 (100 minus 25.17). That is an increase of ₹9.77 on a base of ₹65.06, or about 15%. A 10-point rate cut produces a bigger than 10% jump in profit after tax, because the gain is measured against the smaller after-tax base.

children.text: Four Everyday Decisions That Quietly Set Your Tax Bill

The 2019 cut was a government decision. The more useful lesson for a business owner is how many tax outcomes sit inside decisions the company makes itself, often in departments that never think of themselves as tax-relevant.
1. Structure and regime

Whether you run as a proprietorship, LLP or private limited company decides which rate schedule applies to your profit and how money reaches you personally. For a company, choosing between the concessional 22% regime and the old regime with deductions is a formal choice with long-term consequences. Take a company with ₹12 crore of taxable profit and no significant deductions to claim.

columns.label: Old regime, 30% base rate
points: Can still claim eligible deductions and incentives

columns.label: Concessional 22% regime
points: Gives up most deductions and incentives in exchange

body.label: Annual saving from one regime choice
body.context: For a company with ₹12 crore of taxable profit and few deductions. Chapter 3 shows when the old regime can still win.

children.text: 2. Cash flow timing

markDefs.definition: Income tax paid during the year in instalments on estimated income, instead of in one lump sum after the year ends.

children.text: Companies must pay
advance tax

in four instalments during the year. A treasury team that treats tax as a March problem pays interest for the privilege, and that interest is not deductible. It is a pure leak created by poor planning, not by the tax rate.

body.title: Show me the math: what skipping instalments costs

children.text: A company expects a tax liability of ₹40 lakh for the year. It pays nothing until 15 March, then pays the full ₹40 lakh on that date. Interest for deferring each instalment runs at 1% per month, for three months on each of the first three instalments.

content.caption: Applied to each of the June, September and December instalments
Interest on a ₹40 lakh liability paid entirely on 15 March

children.text: ₹1,62,000 paid for nothing except poor timing. Chapter 4 covers the exact rules, including what happens if even the March instalment is missed.
3. Vendor and purchase discipline

markDefs.definition: The GST you paid on business purchases, which you can offset against the GST you collect on sales, so that tax is only paid on the value you add.

children.text: Under GST, the tax you pay on purchases is recoverable as
input tax credit

, but only if your supplier reports the invoice properly. When a Bengaluru IT services firm buys ₹10 lakh of laptops and pays ₹1.8 lakh of GST at 18%, that ₹1.8 lakh is a recoverable credit if the vendor files correctly, and a straight cost if the vendor does not. The procurement team's choice of vendor, not the tax team, decides which.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Claiming GST Credit
body.textWithBlank: A business can generally claim input tax credit on a purchase only when the supplier's invoice appears in its auto-generated GST statement called ___.
body.explanation: GSTR-2B is the monthly statement of input tax credit available to you, built from what your suppliers report in their own returns. If a supplier's invoice is missing from it, the credit is generally not available until the supplier fixes their filing. Chapter 5 covers this in detail.

children.text: 4. How the company pays people

Salary, bonus, ESOPs, reimbursements and payments to freelancers each carry different tax treatment for the company and for the person receiving the money. HR and L&D teams designing a compensation or benefits policy are, whether they know it or not, making tax decisions on behalf of every employee. Chapter 6 unpacks this.

body.title: Scenario: The Freelancer Nobody Deducted TDS On
body.scenario: A Hyderabad SaaS startup pays a freelance developer ₹4,00,000 over the year for building product features. The operations head processes each invoice in full, without deducting TDS, because "he's not an employee." The startup is a private limited company in the concessional 22% regime.
body.prompt: What has gone wrong, and roughly what could it cost the company in extra income tax alone?
body.modelAnswer: Payments to resident contractors and professionals above the prescribed thresholds require the payer to deduct TDS, whether or not the payee is an employee. When a business fails to deduct or deposit TDS on such a payment, 30% of that expense is disallowed when computing its taxable income for the year. Here, 30% of ₹4,00,000 is ₹1,20,000 added back to taxable profit. At an effective rate of 25.168%, that is about ₹30,202 of extra income tax, before interest on the TDS itself and possible penalties. The disallowed amount can generally be claimed in the year the TDS is eventually deducted and deposited, so the fix is to deduct and deposit it with interest as soon as possible, and to put a TDS check into the invoice approval process. An operations decision created a tax cost.

body.text: Tax rules can also change beneath you. In 2012 India amended its tax law retrospectively to tax Vodafone's 2007 purchase of Hutchison's Indian telecom business, after the Supreme Court had ruled in Vodafone's favour. It took until 2021 for Parliament to scrap such retrospective demands. The lesson for a business owner is to build some tolerance for policy change into long-term plans, and to review your tax position after every Union Budget.

body.title: Recent changes that reshaped business taxation in India

events.title: GST launched
events.description: A single national tax on goods and services replaced excise duty, service tax, VAT and several other levies.

events.title: Concessional corporate tax regime
events.description: Domestic companies could opt for a 22% base rate by giving up most exemptions, taking the effective rate to about 25.17%.

events.title: Dividend Distribution Tax abolished
events.description: Dividends became taxable in shareholders' hands instead of being taxed at the company level before payout.

events.title: Retrospective tax demands scrapped
events.description: Parliament withdrew demands raised under the 2012 retrospective amendment, closing disputes such as Vodafone and Cairn.

events.title: Angel tax removed
events.description: The tax on share premium received by unlisted companies above fair value stopped applying for all classes of investors.

events.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 takes effect
events.description: A rewritten income tax law replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961, introducing the single concept of a tax year and renumbering provisions. Lesson 3 covers what changed.

body.title: Try It: Tax Under the 22% Regime
body.prompt: A Pune-based manufacturer in the concessional 22% regime reports taxable profit of ₹4 crore. Using the effective rate of 25.168%, what is its income tax for the year? Answer in ₹ lakh.
body.explanation: ₹4,00,00,000 × 25.168% = ₹1,00,67,200, which is ₹100.67 lakh. The 25.168% comes from 22% × 1.10 (surcharge) × 1.04 (health and education cess). Under this regime the 10% surcharge applies regardless of the level of income.

children.text: See It in Real Companies

body.title: Find a Listed Company's Tax Rate on screener.in
steps: Open screener.in and search for any large listed company you know, for example a consumer, IT or auto company
Scroll to the Profit & Loss section and find the row labelled Tax %
Compare the last three years against the 25.17% effective rate of the concessional regime

If the figure is noticeably lower or higher, note it down. Tax holidays, SEZ units, losses from earlier years, deferred tax and overseas subsidiaries are common reasons, all covered later in this course
Repeat for a second company in a different sector and compare the two

cards.definition: Tax on income or profit, paid by the entity that earns it. Income tax on company profit is the main example.
Tax on transactions such as sales or imports, collected by the business and ultimately borne by the consumer. GST and customs duty are examples.
The total tax actually charged as a share of taxable profit, after adding surcharge and cess to the base rate.
An additional levy calculated as a percentage of the base income tax, such as 10% under the concessional corporate regime.
A 4% levy on income tax plus surcharge, applicable to companies and individuals alike.
GST paid on business purchases that can be set off against GST collected on sales, if the supplier reports the invoice correctly.
Tax deducted at source. The payer withholds part of certain payments and deposits it with the government on the payee's behalf.

points: Tax on profit takes roughly a quarter to a third of a profitable Indian company's pre-tax earnings, making it one of its largest costs
Businesses face both direct taxes (income tax, advance tax, TDS) and indirect taxes (GST, customs), and act as the government's collection agent for TDS and GST
The September 2019 cut to a 22% base rate lifted after-tax profit by about 15% for companies that opted in, and markets repriced them within hours
Structure and regime choice, advance tax timing, vendor GST compliance and compensation design are everyday decisions that set the final tax bill
Tax mistakes often start outside the finance team, in procurement, operations or HR, so tax awareness is everyone's job
Tax law changes with every Budget and occasionally in larger ways, such as the Income-tax Act, 2025 taking effect from April 2026
